extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners working on long-form story generation
extracted.subtask_description: Learning and evaluating reasoning mechanisms that improve long-form (multi‑chapter) story generation, by framing a Next‑Chapter Prediction task and training with verifiable rewards on unlabeled books. The goal is to produce detailed plans and chapters that better track plot/characters and maintain an engaging, consistent style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking plot and character arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: Generating high-quality stories requires competency in tracking plot and character arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as a core skill necessary for long-form story generation; implicated as an evaluative dimension when assessing chapters produced by the system (i.e., does the generated chapter correctly continue and develop plotlines and character trajectories?).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent and engaging style
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping a consistent and engaging style across long documents is necessary for high-quality stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed alongside plot/character tracking as a required competency; used as an axis of human preference judgments for comparing generated chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Next‑Chapter Prediction (task formulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate story generation as a Next‑Chapter Prediction task: given condensed information about a story, predict/generate the next chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a general story‑generation task that enables learning reasoning from unlabeled books; serves as the principal training/evaluation problem in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verified Rewards via Completion Likelihood Improvement (reward formulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reward formulation (Verified Rewards via Completion Likelihood Improvement) that allows using an unlabeled book dataset as a learning signal for reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reward measures improvement in completion likelihood and is verifiable, enabling reinforcement learning-style training without labeled chapter annotations; presented as central to the method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoning over condensed story information and producing a detailed plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn to reason over a story's condensed information and generate a detailed plan for the next chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producing an explicit detailed plan is part of the system's reasoning capability and an evaluand—quality of reasoning is measured by how well these plans lead to better generated chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate reasoning via downstream chapter quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasoning is evaluated indirectly via the chapters it helps a story-generator create.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than assessing reasoning in isolation, the paper measures the value of learned reasoning by the quality of generated chapters (as judged by human raters and compared to baselines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human pairwise judgments across multiple metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pairwise human judgments to compare generated chapters across metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports pairwise human preference judgments indicating the learned-reasoning chapters are preferred across 'almost all metrics' (metrics not enumerated in the abstract); human pairwise comparison is the primary evaluation protocol reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of unlabeled book dataset as learning signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage an unlabeled book dataset to provide a learning signal for reasoning (motivated by difficulty of sourcing labeled datasets and precise quality measurements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural/data requirement enables training without chapter-level labels by using the Verified Rewards formulation; emphasized as a motivation and methodological constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to non-trained and supervised finetuning (SFT) baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess learned-reasoning models by comparing generated chapters against non-trained models and supervised fine‑tuning baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline comparisons are used to demonstrate empirical gains; reported result is that learned reasoning produces chapters preferred over these baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-specific effectiveness (Sci‑Fi and Fantasy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of learned reasoning is more pronounced in Sci‑Fi and Fantasy genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract notes stronger empirical preference gains in these genres, suggesting genre is an important consideration when evaluating and applying the method.
